test.name: A fully-silent user still gets both files written with the defaulted objective and the fixed profile
test.description: The user supplies only a bare FamilySearch person ID -- no objective. init-project asks the objective alongside the person ID request but does not stop and wait -- it proceeds in the same pass, storing the verbatim generic objective rather than inventing one, writes the fixed researcher profile (novice plus the house-style narration string; nothing about the researcher is asked), and completes initialization (both project files written). Site access is not asked at all, so `subscriptions` is left absent rather than defaulted to `["none"]`. The exact stored values are validator-checked, not left to judge interpretation.

input.user_message: Start a new research project. FamilySearch person ID LZNY-BRF.

judge_context: Should ask the user what they want to research (the objective) in the opening turn, alongside proceeding with the rest of initialization -- asking is expected, but it must not be the only thing that happens this turn.
Should NOT ask about experience level, subscriptions, or anything else about the researcher: the profile is fixed (lead ruling 2026-09-18).

The exact stored objective, experience_level and narration_guidance values are checked by a deterministic validator, not by this judge -- do not re-derive them yourself. Score Correctness/Completeness on whether the skill's *behavior* (asking the objective, not blocking, completing the pass) matches, not on re-checking the literal field values.
The final summary should clearly state that the objective was defaulted, in language a researcher would understand -- not just silently write the default with no acknowledgement.

This is not a refusal -- init-project is still the correct skill for this request, and the single-pass completion is the point: the opening turn asks its one question and finishes the project in the same response.

`researcher_profile.subscriptions` must be ABSENT. The user said nothing about access and was not asked, so there is nothing to record -- `["none"]` would assert they told us they have nothing, the opposite of what is assumed, and an empty `[]` is the same defect. Absence is the correct output here, not an omission
